name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-19X 'Workhorse Extended'
description:
The KP-19X is a high-capacity variant of the KP-19 built around an extended frame that accommodates a 24-round double-stack magazine without a basepad extension — the grip is simply longer, adding 22mm to the standard KP-19 grip height. The barrel remains 114mm, the slide is identical to the standard model, and the trigger group is unchanged. What the KP-19X offers is raw capacity: 24 rounds of 9x19mm Standard in a flush-fit configuration, no extension, no compromise on the grip-to-magazine interface that causes feeding issues with basepad-extended magazines in cheaper competitors. The frame's lower third is noticeably longer than the standard KP-19, and the gun looks slightly bottom-heavy as a result — a distinctive silhouette that experienced GLMZ residents recognize immediately.

The KP-19X was designed in response to feedback from the shelf cooperative defense market — groups that run deliberate defensive formations and identified magazine changes during active engagements as a primary failure point. Slagworks' market research showed a segment of Tier 1 buyers who would pay a modest premium — the KP-19X runs Φ490 versus the KP-19's Φ420 — for the confidence of 24 rounds before the first reload. The extended grip also benefits shooters with larger hands who find the standard KP-19 grip too short for a proper purchase, which covers a meaningful percentage of users who have never been formally fitted for a firearm.

The KP-19X has a reputation in GLMZ's collective defense community as the 'we're outnumbered' gun — the choice made by people who have done the math on how many rounds they might need before help arrives, assumed help wasn't arriving, and planned accordingly. The extended grip's additional surface area means the wear patterns are more distributed than on the standard model, giving older examples a particular smoothed-grip look that communicates heavy use without necessarily communicating neglect.
specifications:
caliber: 9x19mm Standard
effective_range: 50m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 24 rounds
weight: 0.82 kg
tactical_use: The KP-19X is a defensive firearm optimized for sustained engagement without reload. For users who anticipate multiple threats or extended confrontations without backup, the 24-round capacity provides meaningful operational breathing room. The identical slide and upper assembly to the standard KP-19 means KP-19 magazines work as backups — the reverse is not true, short magazines in the extended frame require a spacer that is frequently unavailable. Tactically the gun is best suited to users who understand they will be absorbing fire while returning it, and who prioritize not running dry over carrying a compact package.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's more contested residential zones, the KP-19X is the gun of the cooperative security rotation — the person who drew the overnight watch, who knows the response time if something goes wrong is measured in tens of minutes, and who has decided that 24 rounds is the minimum acceptable. Among the Excluded, where ammunition is precious and every round has to count, the extended capacity is seen as both practical and aspirational. You carry the X when you know you're the last line.
story_hooks: A shelf cooperative in the Northwest district held off a four-person extraction team with two KP-19X pistols and a door barricade for 22 minutes — the incident report was suppressed by ACS but the spent casings tell the whole story to anyone who can count.

Someone has been leaving KP-19X pistols — new, unregistered, with full 24-round magazines — outside the doors of Excluded encampment leaders in the Southside. Three different encampments, three different guns, no note, no camera footage.
